feedback: If a learner names only a healthy state, prompt: 'What if this one were missing — what would you see?'
If a learner lists animal needs for the plant (e.g. a food bowl), revisit that the plant makes its own food from light and does not eat.
Confirm correct need–part pairings and have the learner say the matching consequence.
activities.intendedInsight: Each need is linked to a part or behaviour of the organism and to a specific consequence if it is missing.
learnerActions: Look at a plant and an animal and name each basic need aloud: for the plant — water, light, air, suitable temperature; for the animal — water, food, air, shelter/warmth.
Pair each need with the part or behaviour that uses it, e.g. roots take up water, leaves use light, the animal's mouth takes in food.
For each need, say what the living thing would look like if that need were missing (e.g. 'no water → wilts', 'no light → pale', 'no food → weak').
activities.title: Name the needs and what uses them
